CAT.rationale: CAT's franchise quality is genuinely excellent — dominant dealer network, 35.7% five-year average ROIC, record $63B backlog, and a secular tailwind from data-center power demand that is generating real revenue (Power & Energy now ~47% of sales). Q1 2026 results were outstanding: 22% YoY revenue growth, 19% EPS beat, and management raised both near-term and long-term guidance. However, the stock has been re-rated to an extreme that overwhelms these positives. Trailing PE has expanded from 14x to 42.7x in 12 months — a 3x multiple expansion — while cumulative EPS growth over the same period was only ~16%. The earnings yield of 2.3% sits 210bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.4%, implying a negative equity risk premium for a cyclical industrial. Gross margins are compressing (37.1% → 33.8% over three quarters), tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.6B are a real near-term drag (Resource Industries margin collapsed from 17% to 10%), and the balance sheet carries 3.5x D/E leverage. The stock at $890 is pricing in flawless, perpetual execution with zero margin of safety. Even the Q1 earnings beat — the strongest catalyst available — appears already priced in given the stock's 121% one-year rally and 33.8% quarterly gain into the print. This is a case where excellent fundamentals are rendered unattractive by an extreme, momentum-driven valuation that has pulled forward years of potential earnings growth.
